title: Anand Rathi AM interview
source: Anand Rathi Wealth Account Manager revision guide and company profile notes
purpose: Preparing for an Account Manager (wealth management) interview at Anand Rathi Wealth.
about: Company facts, tax and return maths, fund rules, products and plumbing. Tax rates as of FY2025-26; confirm live rates.

sections.title: The company
sections.why: Expect "what do you know about us?" with follow-ups on people, scale and history.

options: HUL and Deutsche Bank; IIT Kanpur, JBIMS

Why can't you compare today's ₹2,288 with the ₹550 IPO price?

sections.title: Tax maths
sections.why: Tax-aware advice is in your pitch; expect a worked number.

questions.prompt: Raise ₹10 L via FIFO. Lot A: LTCG ₹1.5 L. Lot B: STCG ₹1.2 L. Tax incl. cess?
questions.answer: ₹3,125 + ₹24,000 = ₹27,125; + 4% cess = **₹28,210**. Option: wait till Lot B passes 12 months.

questions.prompt: 30% slab, ₹1.2 L gain in a debt fund after 2 years. Tax incl. cess?
questions.hint: Specified debt fund: holding period doesn't matter.
questions.answer: Same gain in an arbitrage fund after 12 months: **nil** if the ₹1.25 L exemption is unused.

questions.prompt: Equity fund: ₹20 L → ₹26 L in 18 months. Tax incl. cess?
questions.answer: ₹59,375 is right **before** cess; the 4% cess adds ₹2,375.

questions.prompt: Arbitrage fund, gain ₹80,000, held 10 months. Tax before cess?
questions.answer: The ₹1.25 L exemption is for **LTCG** only. Under 12 months → 20% STCG.

questions.prompt: A gold FoF or 35–65% equity fund held 30 months is taxed at…
questions.answer: Short-term (under 24 months) at slab.

questions.prompt: Listed bond held 14 months vs an MLD held 14 months?
questions.answer: Listed bonds go long-term after **12 months**. Unlisted bonds and MLDs: slab regardless.

questions.prompt: Equity bought 2016 at ₹100; 31 Jan 2018 value ₹160; sold ₹140. Cost for tax?
questions.hint: Higher of cost and FMV, capped at sale value.
questions.answer: Higher of ₹100 and ₹160 = ₹160, capped at sale ₹140 → cost **₹140**, gain nil.

questions.prompt: STCL ₹50,000, LTCG ₹2 L this year (equity). Taxable LTCG after set-off and exemption?
questions.answer: STCL sets off against either; LTCL only against LTCG. Carry forward 8 years.

questions.prompt: TDS on IDCW applies at ___ above ___ a year.
questions.answer: IDCW itself is taxed at slab; NAV falls by the payout.

sections.title: Return and risk maths
sections.why: IRR/XIRR and variance vs plan are in the job description itself.

questions.prompt: ₹10 L → ₹15 L in 3 years. CAGR?
questions.answer: Simple averaging (16.67%) overstates compound growth.

questions.prompt: Buy ₹100, ₹5 dividend, sell ₹115. Holding period return?
questions.answer: HPR = (EV − BV + Income)/BV.

questions.prompt: Rp 12%, Rf 6%, σ 10%, β 1.2. Sharpe and Treynor?
questions.answer: Sharpe = 6/10; Treynor = 6/1.2. Use Treynor when the fund sits inside a diversified whole.

questions.prompt: Excess return 6%, downside deviation 8%. Sortino?
questions.answer: Sortino = (Rp − Rf or MAR)/downside deviation.

questions.prompt: Rp 15, Rf 6, Rm 12, β 1.2. Jensen's alpha?
questions.answer: 3 is **simple** alpha (vs benchmark). Jensen's measures against CAPM's expected 13.2%.

questions.prompt: Rp 14, Rb 11, tracking error 3. Information ratio?
questions.hint: Active return per unit of active risk.
questions.answer: Use IR, alpha and tracking error for an active fund vs its index.

questions.prompt: Which is beta?
questions.answer: Dividing by Var(Rp) is a common slip. β 1.2, market +10% → about +12%.

questions.prompt: Client added ₹50 L just before a 15% fall. TWR vs XIRR?
questions.answer: TWR strips out flow timing (judges the manager); XIRR is money-weighted (client's experience).

questions.prompt: ₹1 Cr portfolio: equity ₹68 L vs 60% target. Amount to move to restore target?
questions.answer: +8 pts on ₹1 Cr = **₹8 L**. Use new money and SIPs first; check tax and exit loads.

questions.prompt: NAV with ₹100 cr assets, ₹2 cr liabilities, 4.9 cr units?
questions.answer: NAV = (assets − liabilities)/units. Expense ratio is already inside it.

sections.title: Capture ratios and fund rules
sections.why: Your Dezerv strengths: they'll test depth, not definitions.

questions.prompt: Benchmark −3% in down months; fund −2.1%. Downside capture?
questions.answer: Below 100 = falls less than the market.

questions.prompt: Fund A: 110/105. Fund B: 85/60. Better capture ratio?
questions.answer: B is defensive but gives up far less on falls; suits a cautious 55-year-old.

questions.prompt: Upside 120, downside 115. Reading?
options: Ideal: beats on rises, protects on falls
questions.answer: Ideal needs downside **below** 100.

questions.prompt: Balanced hybrid fund is usually taxed as…
questions.answer: Aggressive hybrid (65–80% equity) is equity-taxed. Always check the actual mix.

questions.prompt: Equity savings fund rule?
questions.answer: Equity taxation with conservative net equity exposure.

questions.prompt: Large & mid cap vs multi cap rule?
options: L&M: ≥35% each large, mid; Multi: ≥25% each L, M, S
questions.answer: Multi cap holds 75% minimum in equity across caps; flexi cap ≥65% equity, any cap.

questions.prompt: Corporate bond fund vs credit risk fund?
options: ≥80% AA+ and above vs ≥65% AA and below
questions.answer: Banking & PSU: ≥80% banks/PSUs/PFIs. Gilt: ≥80% G-secs (no credit, high rate risk).

questions.prompt: Short duration fund's Macaulay duration?
questions.answer: Liquid: maturity up to 91 days; overnight: 1-day paper.

questions.prompt: Purchase cut-off for liquid and overnight funds?
questions.answer: Most other purchases and redemptions: 3 pm. Liquid funds have a graded exit load for 7 days.

questions.prompt: Index fund / ETF: ≥___ in index constituents; watch ___.
questions.answer: Tracking difference is the return gap; tracking error is its volatility.

sections.title: Products: bonds, REITs, structured, PMS/AIF
sections.why: Structured products and alternatives are on ARWL's shelf and are your stated gap.

questions.prompt: ₹100 face, 8% coupon, price ₹95. Current yield?
questions.answer: 8% is the coupon rate. YTM would also count the ₹5 pull to par.

questions.prompt: Mod. duration 6, yields fall 0.5%. Price moves about…
questions.answer: Rates down, prices up.

questions.prompt: Lowest investment-grade rating?
questions.answer: BB and below is speculative. Agencies: CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, India Ratings.

questions.prompt: AT1 bank bonds sit where, and what's the case to cite?
options: Below senior debt; can be written off (Yes Bank 2020)
questions.answer: IL&FS, DHFL and Franklin Templeton are credit-stress examples, not AT1 write-offs.

questions.prompt: REIT leverage: cap and approval trigger?
options: Cap 49%; above 25% needs AAA + unitholder approval
questions.answer: Plus ≥90% NDCF distributed; REITs ≥80% in completed, rent-generating assets.

questions.prompt: Which REIT distribution component is NOT income?
questions.answer: It reduces unit cost. Interest is slab-taxed; dividend depends on the SPV's tax regime.

questions.prompt: Sale of listed REIT/InvIT units is taxed like…
options: Listed equity: 20% short / 12.5% long above ₹1.25 L
questions.answer: Verify the current rule.

questions.prompt: Protected note: Nifty +40%, 80% participation, no cap. Payoff on ₹1 Cr?
questions.answer: 0.8 × 40% = 32%. Nifty −30% → principal back **only if** the issuer pays and you hold to maturity.

questions.prompt: An MLD's investor carries which risk even if the index rallies?
questions.answer: Usually an NBFC issuer. Also lock-in, illiquidity, capped upside, slab tax.

questions.prompt: AIF Category III vs I/II taxation?
options: Cat III taxed at fund level; I and II mostly pass-through
Cat I taxed at fund level; II, III pass-through
Investor taxed per trade in all
questions.answer: PMS: securities in your demat, taxed per transaction. Angel funds: ₹25 L minimum.

questions.prompt: Which AIF category fits private credit and real estate?
questions.answer: Cat I: startups, infra, SME. Cat III: hedge-style, leverage allowed.

sections.title: Plumbing: CAS, KYC, AA
sections.why: Documentation and client queries are a big share of the AM's week.

questions.prompt: A client holds MF units in demat and in folios. To see everything you need…
options: Both depository CAS and RTA CAS
MF Central alone covers demat shares
questions.answer: Depository CAS: demat holdings incl. demat MF units. RTA CAS: folio units across AMCs.

questions.prompt: Depository CAS is sent when?
questions.answer: Comes as Summary or Detailed.

questions.prompt: Who runs the CKYC registry?
questions.answer: KRAs include CVL, NDML, CAMS, KFin, DotEx.

questions.prompt: In Account Aggregator, an RTA or bank is the ___ and the adviser the ___.
questions.answer: Financial Information Provider → (data-blind AA) → Financial Information User.

questions.prompt: Which can freeze an MF folio?
options: Missing FATCA, nomination, mobile or email
questions.answer: Nomination needs a choice or an opt-out declaration.

questions.prompt: An edge of demat MF units over folio units?
questions.answer: Demat units carry an ISIN; easier transmission too.

questions.prompt: RIA vs distributor: registration and pay?
options: RIA: SEBI, fee-based fiduciary; distributor: AMFI ARN, commission
questions.answer: Distributors also need NISM certification. Don't assert ARWL's category.
